title: Product Launch Social Listening: A Before, During, After Plan
summary: A product launch social listening plan: queries and a baseline before launch, a launch-week watch list, and a post-launch review, with an owner for each phase.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Product launch social listening works as three phases, each with a named decision owner and a defined metric: record a baseline before launch (a new product name has no history, so start brand, category and claim queries early), watch a short list of themes in launch week, then compare against the baseline in a review. A listening tool shows the conversation, and your team decides what to do about it. The phases, owners and timing are our suggested approach.


Switch on product launch social listening on launch day and you start with no baseline, no owner for each theme and no way to tell which post deserves a phone call.


The launch guidance we opened agrees on a sequence: baseline, watch, compare. The pages we opened do not publish owners per phase, metric formulas or a rehearsal.


Without those, a claim people dispute or a stock-out complaint can sit in a dashboard with no one assigned to act.


This post adds a three-phase plan with an owner, metrics and an output for each phase, plus a pre-launch rehearsal, as our suggested approach.


## What is product launch social listening, and what does it add to a launch plan?


Product launch social listening adds a baseline to compare against and a route from each signal to a person who can act.


**Product launch social listening** : monitoring public social conversation about a new product, its brand, its category, its claims and the creators seeding it, across a baseline before launch, a watch during launch week and a review afterward. (Our definition.)


**Baseline** : the average statistics you record, such as weekday and weekend daily volume, weekly and monthly volume, typical sentiment, top keywords and top outlets. Carma advises against baselining on a noisy period, such as the weeks after a celebrity mentions your product. (Source:[Carma, Dec 12, 2022](https://carma.com/ar/tms/why-establishing-a-baseline-is-important) )


**Decision owner** : the one role that can change something based on a listening signal, named in advance with a backup. (Our definition.)


The tool is only the collection layer; for video-first launches, that layer is[video social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) .


## What does a product launch social listening plan look like by phase?


Three phases: Before sets up queries and a baseline, During watches a short list of themes, and After compares against the baseline and records decisions. Our suggested boundaries: Before ends at sign-off, about a week before launch day; During runs from launch day through launch week; After starts once launch week ends.


Before


During


After


**Goal**


Know what normal looks like


See confusion, claim challenges and availability or price friction fast enough to route them


Learn what changed and what to carry forward


**Decision owner (role)**


Listening lead (queries, baseline); product marketing (claim sheet); launch lead signs off


Launch lead (messaging); an owner and backup per theme; one person runs check-ins


Launch lead chairs; theme owners report; listening lead owns the next baseline


**Metric definitions**


Daily volume by platform; theme mix (share of mentions per theme); sentiment mix on a person-checked sample; share of a sample marked relevant


Volume against baseline, same window; share of mentions that are questions; share disputing a claim; credible defect reports (count); seeded posts with and without disclosure; hours to owner acknowledgment


Change in volume, theme mix and sentiment mix on the same definitions; new language; share of questions answered; decisions with dates


**Output**


Query book, baseline sheet, owner map, rehearsal log, sign-off


Written status per check-in, incident log


One-page learning review, open items, next baseline


None of these metrics has a target: we found no source for a spike size, a lift or a target sentiment share, so measure against your own baseline.


## Before launch: how do you set up product launch social listening queries and a baseline?


We suggest building separate queries by purpose, starting them well before launch, and rehearsing your alert rules on a window you can replay. A new product name has no history, so your baseline lives in the brand, category, competitor and claim queries.


Separate queries let each alert map to one owner; this set is our suggested approach, not tested as Boolean logic.

Bulldog Reporter, published by Agility PR Solutions, suggests setting a baseline before the first announcement, then reviewing the prior 7 to 14 days for typical daily volume, recurring themes and who mentions the brand when nothing is promoted, and the prior 30 to 60 days for seasonality. (Source:[Bulldog Reporter, Feb 27, 2026](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/crisis-comms-media-monitoring/advanced-media-monitoring-for-e-commerce-launches-what-to-track/) ) That is one publisher's suggestion, with no method shown.


Whether a baseline can be built after a query exists depends on the tool and platform. Two vendors list no history or no backfill for TikTok and for Instagram hashtag or topic collection, and Meta's API limits hashtag search to the last 24 hours, so we suggest collecting forward from the day each query starts. For the wider comparison, see[what historical data means](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-historical-data-what-12-tools-mean-(2026)) .

**Shadow rehearsal** : running dashboards and alert rules before launch so results go only to the rule's author or a digest, then having a person mark each result act now, read later or ignore. (Our definition.)


We suggest running it on a window you can replay: a previous launch of your own, a rival's recent launch, or the quiet days of your new queries. Tune queries and filters first, then grouping, then sensitivity; our[alert budget approach](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-alert-fatigue-how-many-alerts-is-too-many) covers the method. Finish with a tabletop drill, such as a scripted claim challenge, to test the path from sighting to approver.


Before sign-off, we suggest a claim sheet, an owner map, and a "not in view" list of places your tool may not collect: DMs, closed groups, retailer-site reviews and care tickets. For the full list of pre-launch gaps, see[VoC blind spots before launch](https://syncly.app/blog/voc-blind-spots-before-product-launch) .


## Launch week: what should the team watch, and who decides?


We suggest watching a short, stable list of themes, with a named owner and a backup for each. The launch lead decides on messaging.


Bulldog Reporter suggests a small stable topic set: product promise, pricing and promotions, trust and safety claims, shipping and availability, comparisons and creator framing. It says the goal is consistency, not perfect categorization, and suggests one designated person checking about twice a day. (Source:[Bulldog Reporter, Feb 27, 2026](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/crisis-comms-media-monitoring/advanced-media-monitoring-for-e-commerce-launches-what-to-track/) ) Pulsar adds messaging misreads and engagement from unexpected audiences as launch signals. (Source:[Pulsar, Apr 24, 2026](https://www.pulsarplatform.com/guides/social-listening-for-campaign-planning) )

We suggest one agreed time zone, a written status after each check-in and an incident log outside the tool. In our approach, a theme that never triggers a decision is a dashboard item, not a launch-week alert.


Hypothetical example: a beauty brand launches a new serum, and the question "is it the same formula?" barely appears in baseline week. In launch week it becomes a visible share of mentions, so product marketing posts a clarifying line.


We suggest treating a credible safety or defect claim as always-escalate, and mapping every theme to your own tiers. Our[5-stage crisis framework](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-for-crisis-management-a-5-stage-framework) covers triage, owners and approvals if a launch issue becomes a crisis.


Pulsar says the first 24 hours are when intervention is most effective on messaging misreads, and that after 48 hours the reframing often becomes the dominant interpretation. That is a vendor assertion with no evidence shown. (Source:[Pulsar, Apr 24, 2026](https://www.pulsarplatform.com/guides/social-listening-for-campaign-planning) )


For seeded creator content, the FTC's Endorsement Guides Q&A is staff guidance, not a safe harbor. It says receiving free products can call for a disclosure, that a brand sending a gifted product should ask for disclosure and monitor tagged posts, and that each post needing a disclosure should carry its own. (Source:[FTC, undated, checked Oct 2026](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking) ) This is not legal advice.


For which creator roles to recruit, see[creator types for launches](https://syncly.app/blog/creator-types-b2c-product-launches) .


## After launch: how do you run the learning review?


We suggest one scheduled review after launch week: compare launch data with the baseline on the same definitions, and end with decisions and owners.


Pulsar's post-campaign list covers net sentiment change, which communities engaged and whether they were the intended ones, new language and competitive response. Bulldog Reporter suggests a recap that explains spikes by operational causes, such as inventory or shipping changes, and uses a few defensible metrics. (Sources:[Pulsar, Apr 24, 2026](https://www.pulsarplatform.com/guides/social-listening-for-campaign-planning) ;[Bulldog Reporter, Feb 27, 2026](https://www.agilitypr.com/pr-news/crisis-comms-media-monitoring/advanced-media-monitoring-for-e-commerce-launches-what-to-track/) ) Our suggested agenda:


-


Compare volume, theme mix and sentiment mix against the baseline, with sentiment checked on a sample first.


-


List themes that entered or grew, communities that engaged, unanswered questions and competitor responses.


-


Match spikes to causes: stock, shipping, price display, creator posts.


-


Record each decision with an owner and a date, and hand findings to product, marketing, care and creators.


We suggest saving the launch window as a replay set for your next rehearsal, not as the next baseline, because a launch is an unusual period of the kind Carma advises against baselining on.


AMEC's Integrated Evaluation Framework gives the review a structure. It separates seven stages: objectives, inputs, activities, outputs, out-takes, outcomes and impact. It says measurement should start from organizational objectives, benchmarks should be set before a campaign, and counting outputs alone measures only part of the activity. (Source:[AMEC, undated, checked Oct 2026](https://amecorg.com/amecframework/) )


Our mapping: objectives are your written decisions, inputs are the query book and claim sheet, and activities are teasers and creator seeding. Listening supplies outputs (volume, reach) and out-takes (questions, engagement), and indicates outcomes, such as claims repeated, doubted or reframed. Impact needs sales, returns and care data, so listening adds context but does not prove it.


## What can product launch social listening data tell you, and what can it not?


It can show what people said in public and how that changed against your baseline. It cannot prove sales impact, and it cannot see everything.


-


**Sentiment:** the launch guidance we opened publishes no sentiment accuracy figures, so do not assume a vendor's label is right. We suggest a person labels a sample of mentions per theme, compares it with the tool's label, and treats sentiment as a triage input.


-


**Blind spots:** we suggest adding queries for product terms people say or show, not only the brand name.


## Key Takeaways


-


Run launch listening in three phases, each with an owner, metric definitions and an output; the timing is our suggested approach.


-


Start queries early and collect forward: a new product name has no history, and some platforms document no backfill.


-


Watch a short, stable list of themes in launch week, and rehearse the route from sighting to owner first.


-


Check sentiment on a sample by hand; listening is evidence of conversation, not proof of impact.


Treat product launch social listening as three phases with owners and definitions, not a dashboard you switch on at launch. A listening tool shows the conversation; people decide what to do about it.
